title: Finite-dimensional derived coproduct preservation from acyclic sums of injectives
statement: Let C,D be abelian categories with derived categories and K-injective resolutions, with C Grothendieck abelian and having classical injective resolutions. Let F:C→D be additive and left exact. Fix a set J such that J-indexed coproducts exist in C,D and F preserves them. Suppose R^qF(X)=0 for every X and q>d, for a single natural number d. Suppose every J-indexed coproduct of injective objects of C is F-acyclic. Then the ordinary unbounded right derived functor RF preserves J-indexed coproducts. It is enough to assume acyclicity of injective sums; closure of all acyclic objects under sums is not required.

source.place: Lemma lemma-finite-cd-mod-n-direct-sums, Tag 0F11, proof of (1); its abstract K-injective/acyclic-complex argument, isolated from the geometric coefficient specialization.

proof.text: Choose for each derived object its functorial K-injective representative. These representatives have injective components. Their termwise coproduct represents the derived coproduct, because C is Grothendieck and coproducts are exact.

Each component of this coproduct is isomorphic to the coproduct of the corresponding injective components. The hypothesis makes it F-acyclic. Each representative separately also has F-acyclic components, since injectives are acyclic.

Use the proved source-library finite-dimension comparison isIso_rightDerivedFunctorUnit_app_of_rightAcyclic: for each of these complexes the canonical map Q(FK)→RF(QK) is invertible without a boundedness assumption. Define the comparison using quotientCompQhIso and rightDerivedFunctorUnit. Its naturality is the unit naturality together with the quotient-comparison naturality.

F preserves the degreewise coproduct, and passage to the derived category preserves this coproduct. Transfer its universal property along the comparison isomorphisms on all representatives and their coproduct. Naturality identifies the transported injections with the actual RF images of coprojections. This proves preservation of the derived coproduct, also for an empty family.

lean.statement:
theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_rightDerivedFunctor_of_injectiveCoproducts
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} C]
    [HasInjectiveResolutions C] [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions D] (J : Type*)
    [HasColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) C] [HasColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) D]
    [PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) F] (d : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ (X : C) (q : ℕ), d < q → IsZero ((F.rightDerived q).obj X))
    (hJ : ∀ X : J → C, (∀ j, Injective (X j)) → F.rightAcyclic (∐ X)) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) F.rightDerivedFunctor
